title: Seastone - Console usage insights & cost mapping
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Seastone through the Console routes and usage analytics, focusing on per-route cost attribution, tagging, and alerting. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated capacity for a forecasted 50% increase in inference traffic and needs clear unit economics and auditability. Agreed to run a shortbench (30k tokens) and share security pack; follow-ups include pricing for committed capacity and a metrics export sample.
action_items: Priya Shah (SE): share route-level CSV export example and cost workbook (due 2026-04-14)
Alex Rivera (AE): send preliminary committed capacity pricing + sample contract language (due 2026-04-15)
Ben Carter (Customer): provide typical route names and peak qps for PO C scoping (due 2026-04-13)
next_steps: Schedule dedicated pilot benchmark (30k tokens, variety of seq lengths)
Share SOC 2 + data residency docs link
Set up 1:1 with FinOps to review per-route cost model
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ben Carter (Seastone), Laila N'Goma (Seastone), Omar Ruiz (Seastone), Speaker 4

Summary (auto): Quick demo of Console usage dashboards, deep dive into per-route cost mapping and alerts, outline of next steps.

00:00 Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We are going to walk through the Console usage view and specifically per-route costs and cost mapping, and then take questions.
00:12 Ben Carter: Yep thanks Alex. We were hoping to see how we can attribute spend back to teams and, uh, figure out hot routes before costs blow up.
00:20 Priya Shah: Totally. I'll share my screen in a second. Couple of things up front, are you running with any batching or prefix caching today?
00:30 Laila N'Goma: We have some prefix caching in our in-house layer, but not at the inference service; most of our requests are short chat style sequences, so batching is limited.
00:38 Omar Ruiz: And from FinOps side, our ask is clear per-route chargebacks for product teams, and a way to show unit cost per 1k tokens. Also automated alerts if a route deviates more than 20%.
00:50 Priya Shah: Great. On screen now — Console home, usage tab. Top-level is token volume, cost over time, and you can group by route, model, or team tag.
01:05 Speaker 4: Sorry can you zoom into the per-route breakdown?
01:10 Priya Shah: Sure. Here is per-route — we show total tokens, serving cost, and latency p50/p95. Notice you can switch charge model to "token-only" or "token + infra" to include dedicated GPU ops.
01:25 Alex Rivera: An important callout: the cost column uses our Optimize recommendations if you enable it — so if you have quantized model variants it can suggest using them and show projected savings.
01:35 Ben Carter: Is the projected savings a simulation or based on your dedicated telemetry?
01:40 Priya Shah: It's a mix. We run historical replay and kernel-level throughput models — sometimes we call out that it's an estimate. We also annotate the confidence band.
01:55 Laila N'Goma: How granular are the tags? Our infra team wants to map routes to kubernetes namespaces, service names, and product squads.
02:05 Priya Shah: You can attach up to four tags per route; we map route -> service -> namespace via route annotations. Also we support importing a CSV of mappings.
02:18 Omar Ruiz: For chargeback, we need exportable reports — CFO wants monthly per-team ledger.
02:25 Priya Shah: Export CSV / BigQuery push is built-in. You can schedule daily exports to a GCS bucket or S3, and include raw route metrics and cost breakdown.
02:35 Ben Carter: Sweet. Could we see an example where a route suddenly had a cost spike?
02:40 Priya Shah: Yeah I'll pull a demo route. Here we have Route: chat-order-fulfill — spike mid-March; Console shows a breadcrumb — originated from a model rollout and fallback to a larger variant.
02:55 Alex Rivera: This is where our rollouts and fallback policies help. If a canary fails or latency spikes, Redwood can automatically route to a cheaper compatible variant — we log the switch and cost delta.
03:10 Laila N'Goma: Do you keep audit logs for those routing changes? Need them for compliance.
03:15 Priya Shah: Yes — all routing decisions, rollouts, and fallbacks are stored in the audit trail with timestamps and user IDs. We also send them to your SIEM if you configure the integration.
03:28 Omar Ruiz: About dedicated vs hosted — we might want dedicated GPUs for predictable throughput. How does the console show blended costs if some routes hit dedicated and others hosted?
03:38 Priya Shah: The route cost model shows segment-level costs: if a request is served by a dedicated pool, we mark that token allocation as "dedicated" and apply reserved unit pricing. The dashboard has a filter to show only dedicated consumption.
03:50 Ben Carter: Are burst costs handled differently? We want to allow occasional bursts without big commitments.
03:55 Alex Rivera: You can configure reserved capacity with burstable overlay and define a policy that offloads excess to hosted at a different price. The Console will show the blended bill and simulate savings under different commit levels.
04:10 Speaker 4: There's a mention of KV cache in your docs — we use large context windows — how does that show up in costs?
04:18 Priya Shah: Good question. KV cache hits are treated as cache hit savings and we show token-level effective cost reduction. One caveat: speech-to-text in transcriber sometimes writes it as K V cash in our internal logs, so forgive the weird label in older exports.
04:35 Ben Carter: (laughs) noted.
04:40 Priya Shah: Also, you can set alerts: threshold on cost per route, token per minute, or latency p95. Alerts integrate to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.
04:52 Omar Ruiz: For FinOps, can alerts be tied to a budget so we auto-disable non-essential routes?
04:58 Alex Rivera: Yes — you can map routes to budget categories and a policy can limit non-critical routes once budget burns past threshold; it's reversible.
05:10 Laila N'Goma: Security — can we run the private control plane in our VPC and still get Console telemetry? We have strict data residency rules in EU.
05:22 Priya Shah: You can run Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane in your VPC; telemetry can be forwarded to your analytics endpoint, and audit logs remain in-region. We'll also support customer KMS so keys never leave your environment.
05:36 Ben Carter: Great. Can you share the SOC2 and penetration test reports?
05:40 Alex Rivera: We'll share the security pack after the call. I'll include SOC 2 and our latest pentest summary and architecture diagram.
05:48 Speaker 4: On the cost modeling, how accurate are the per-token chargebacks when models have dynamic tokenization (e.g. different tokenizers between models)?
05:56 Priya Shah: We attribute cost at token granularity but normalize tokens to a common unit per model family — so you can compare apples to apples. We call out normalization assumptions in the export.
06:10 Ben Carter: PCI/PII considerations — we need an option to redact transcripts and not retain raw prompts.
06:17 Priya Shah: You can enable prompt redaction and set retention policies per route. We also offer plan-level retention windows for hosted APIs.
06:25 Omar Ruiz: Back to the demo — can we walk through setting an alert for a route and simulating a spike?
06:30 Priya Shah: Sure — creating an alert. Condition: route == chat-order-fulfill, cost increase > 20% in 1h, action: send to Slack + trigger auto-fallback to smaller model. Now I'll simulate.
06:50 (sound of simulated events)
07:05 Priya Shah: The alert fired, and you can see the trace of fallback in the timeline. The cost delta is estimated at 36% savings per hour.
07:20 Ben Carter: Nice. Can we get the raw trace for our audit?
07:24 Priya Shah: Yes — download JSON of timeline events or export to your observability (Datadog/Tempo) via webhook.
07:34 Laila N'Goma: We want to try a pilot with a single route to validate savings. What's typical time for a pilot?
07:40 Alex Rivera: We usually run a 1–2 week pilot depending on traffic; for bench we can do accelerated replay with a 30k token sample to project savings more quickly.
07:52 Ben Carter: Sounds good. What's the expected reduction if we enable KV caching + quantized variants? Ballpark.
07:58 Priya Shah: On chat-like routes with high prefix repetition you often see 30–60% token cost reduction from caching plus another 10–30% from int8 or bfloat16 quantized variants, depending on model fidelity needs.
08:14 Omar Ruiz: Pricing question — if we commit to reserved capacity, do you offer sliding discounts as commit grows?
08:20 Alex Rivera: Yes, our Dedicated pricing has tiers — monthly committed vGPU hours with discounts at each band. We'll propose a recommendation based on your projected peak.
08:30 Ben Carter: Could you provide an example workbook that shows blended cost at different commit levels?
08:35 Priya Shah: I'll attach the workbook — it's the same CSV export we discussed but prefilled with sample rates.
08:42 Speaker 4: Are there rate limits at route level that could skew metrics?
08:46 Priya Shah: You can set per-route rate limits; Console shows the throttled requests as a metric so you'll know.
08:55 Ben Carter: For the pilot, we need an NDA and pricing estimate. Also security docs.
09:01 Alex Rivera: We'll send the NDA and the pilot pricing. We'll also include a sample contract with data residency clauses.
09:08 Laila N'Goma: One more — does the Console support annotating routes with internal owners and sys links?
09:14 Priya Shah: Yes, metadata fields include owner, squad, slack channel, runbook link. You can bulk-edit via CSV.
09:22 Omar Ruiz: Any limitations on historical retention for per-route metrics? We like to keep 13 months for accounting.
09:28 Priya Shah: Standard retention is 90 days in the UI, but exports and longer retention as an add-on for 13 months are supported for enterprise customers.
09:38 Ben Carter: Who should we loop in from Redwood for the pilot setup?
09:42 Alex Rivera: Myself and Priya will run the pilot; we'll also loop in Solutions Eng if we need infra changes.
09:48 Speaker 4: quick note, I saw in older exports some typos where KV cache became K V cash — minor but just a heads up for parsing.
09:57 Priya Shah: We've been cleaning up parser aliases, but thanks for flagging.
10:05 Alex Rivera: Okay let's jump to questions. Omar?
10:08 Omar Ruiz: How do you bill for test/profiling runs — e.g., the 30k token replay?
10:13 Priya Shah: Test runs are billed at hosted rates unless run in a dedicated pool you control. For pilot we can offer a credit to offset the bench cost.
10:24 Ben Carter: Example CSV fields please — route, tokens, cost, model, pool type, timestamp, owner. Anything else?
10:31 Priya Shah: Also include tags, project id, and normalized token unit.
10:36 Alex Rivera: Recap: Redwood to share security pack, workbook, export example; Seastone to send route list and traffic profile; schedule pilot.
10:47 Ben Carter: Agreed. We'll aim to provide route list by Tuesday.
10:52 Alex Rivera: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
10:57 Priya Shah: One last note — the Console can surface recommendations from Optimize, e.g., suggested quantization profiles per model and expected quality delta from evals. It's a link into our evals system.
11:12 Laila N'Goma: That'll be helpful to baseline quality regressions.
11:18 Ben Carter: Thanks everyone.
11:21 Alex Rivera: Thanks — we'll send materials shortly.
11:25 (meeting ends)

Post-call notes: Redwood to attach security docs link, pilot pricing, and CSV export; customer to provide route list and traffic profile.
